newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Asian electronics exports seen slowing - ADB.
newsitem.headline: Asian electronics exports seen slowing - ADB.

text.p: The surge in global computer demand which fueled the meteoric rise of Asian exports in the 1990s, may start to slow as fewer new products come onto the market, the Asian Development Bank said on Thursday.
"In the absence of major new products coming onstream,the industry is unlikely to return to its pre-1996 boom years," the Manila-based bank said in its annual report.
"But with continuing growth in the global economy, demand and supply should come into line with each other and the basis for profitable business should be restored," it added.
During the 1990s, Asia's export boom was highlighted by the growth of high-technology electronics.
The bank noted that Singapore makes about 40 percent of the world's disc drives while one-third of personal computer (PC) micro-processors are packaged and tested in Malaysia.
But last year's slowdown in the world electronics trade hit export growth in the region, with South Korea, Singapore, Malaysia and Taiwan the biggest losers.

"In the short term, Asia's electronics producers will face a demand upturn following inventory adjustment. However, growth is likely to be moderate in the absence of new watershed innovations of the magnitude of the compact disc player or the PC,' it added.
